script.text: Yemen's government just pulled back from the Red Sea's gateway. Is Aden next?

The gateway is Bab al-Mandeb, a strait on the main sea route between Asia and Europe. On Sunday, Yemen's Saudi-backed government said its forces were leaving nearby areas, including Dhubab, to defend the city of Aden.

The Houthis are pushing east. Five Yemeni military personnel told Reuters the rebels reached Khor Omairah, about one hundred kilometres west of Aden. Military sources quoted by AFP put them within sixty kilometres. Government sources say defending Aden is now the priority.

Saudi Arabia reacted on Monday. A royal decree removed the commander of the coalition's joint forces, the Saudi Press Agency reported. Chief of staff Fayyad al-Ruwaili takes over. Reuters says the Houthis have taken swathes of land since the Iran war revived Yemen's civil war this summer.
Will Aden stay in government hands through the winter? Yes or no?

upload.title: Yemen Pulls Back From Bab al-Mandeb. Is Aden Next? #shorts
upload.description:
Yemen's internationally recognised, Saudi-backed government said on Sunday, November 15, 2026, that its forces were withdrawing from Dhubab and areas near the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, one of the world's key shipping chokepoints between the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden, in order to defend Aden, the government's interim seat. Reuters reported that the forces redeployed to al-Suqyah, south of Dhubab. Five Yemeni military personnel told Reuters that Houthi fighters reached the coastal area of Khor Omairah, about 100 km west of Aden; military sources quoted by AFP said the Houthis were within about 60 km of the city. The figures may describe different points of the front and the front line is not independently verified; positions in the video are approximate. Three government sources told Reuters that securing Aden and Lahj province is now the priority. On Monday, November 16, a royal decree reported by the Saudi Press Agency relieved Lt. Gen. Fahd bin Hamad Al-Salman as commander of the coalition's joint forces and appointed him adviser to the defence minister; Chief of the General Staff Fayyad al-Ruwaili takes over the command in addition to his post. No official reason was given. According to Reuters, the Houthis have seized swathes of territory since the US-Iran conflict reignited Yemen's frozen civil war this summer. There was no immediate Houthi comment reported on the pullback.
